subject: AWS Marketplace listing: product description and pricing Q&A
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Morris <sarah.morris@aws-partner.com>, marketplace-ops@aws.amazon.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace listing: product description and pricing Q&A

Hi Sarah / Marketplace team —

Thanks again for the quick onboarding call earlier. Per our action items, attaching the updated listing draft and current pricing tiers for review. Two things we need to lock down this week so we can publish the listing and start co-sell enablement:

1) Final product description (short summary + 2-line technical blurb) that complies with AWS Marketplace guidelines. We cut a ~75-word short description in the attached doc; want PMM sign-off.
2) Pricing structure: we have two candidate SKUs: "Redwood Inference - Standard" (per-token rate) and "Redwood Inference - Dedicated" (monthly reserved throughput). AWS asked whether we can split per-usage vs. commit billing in the listing or if we should surface one primary pricing and link to a doc.

Attachments: redwood_aws_listing_v2.docx, pricing_table_v3.csv

Would appreciate any compliance/ops flags and whether marketplace-ops needs alternative SKU naming to meet merchandising rules.

Thanks —
Jasmine
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai

From: Sarah Morris <sarah.morris@aws-partner.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace onboarding checklist

Hi Jasmine —

Quick note: marketplace-ops prefers single MSRP per listing with an "Additional pricing" doc for complex offers. Co-sell enablement needs the short description live so we can create the partner overview card. Happy to review once you drop the doc.

Best,

AWS Partner Programs

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace listing: product description and pricing Q&A

J -- quick pass below. I put inline suggestions in the doc but also paste the recommended short description for speed: 

[Suggested 72-word short description]
Redwood Inference is a high-throughput LLM serving platform that delivers predictable latency and cost controls for production applications. Available as a hosted API and dedicated private deployments, Redwood optimizes throughput with smart batching, KV caching, and quantization-aware runtimes. Designed for engineering teams building latency-sensitive features, the platform supports streaming responses, function calling integration, and detailed per-route observability.

Notes:
- Remove vendor claims like "lowest" or performance numbers unless referencing a benchmark and link to it.
- For the tech blurb (2 lines) use: "GPU-optimized inference runtime with adaptive batching and model variant routing."

I also recommend listing the Reserved SKU as "Redwood Inference — Dedicated (monthly commit)" and the usage SKU as "Redwood Inference — On-demand (per-token)" to keep naming consistent with Marketplace norms.

- Lauren
Director, Product Marketing

-----Original Message-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace listing: product description and pricing Q&A

Adding SE perspective: make sure the tech blurb calls out regions and supported instance types (we should list T4, A10G, H100 variants supported by Dedicated). Also flag that our per-token pricing has a different unit for embeddings vs. generation — Marketplace typically wants a single metric. Propose we map to "per 1K tokens" for generation and a separate SKU for embeddings.

Karthik
Sales Engineer

-----Original Message-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Sarah Morris <sarah.morris@aws-partner.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace listing: product description and pricing Q&A

Looping in partner ops notes from last co-sell sync: AWS co-sell needs a 1-page partner brief and a consolidated URL to the pricing doc. Sarah: can Marketplace ops accept a shared S3 link for the pricing doc during initial listing, or do you require the doc hosted in the partner portal?

Marcus Lin
Head of Partnerships

-----Original Message-----
From: Sarah Morris <sarah.morris@aws-partner.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace listing: product description and pricing Q&A

Marcus — S3 link is fine for the initial review but eventual co-sell package should be a stable doc in the partner portal. Marketplace-ops will accept temporary links while the listing is in draft. Make sure the pricing doc clearly labels partner-discounted commit rates vs. public MSRP.

Also, the marketplace team wants the short description trimmed to 60-80 words and no HTML tags. If you want I can give a quick copy pass on the marketplace product overview card once you publish the draft in the partner console.

-Sarah

-----Original Message-----
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme-analytics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 08:13:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace listing: product description and pricing Q&A

Jasmine / team —

Quick procurement Qs from our side before we link the purchase order to the Marketplace SKU:

1) For the Dedicated monthly commit SKU, do you provide an invoice that itemizes GPU hours vs. software fee? Our finance team needs a split for internal chargeback.
2) Is there a minimum term for the Dedicated commit? We typically need 12 months but want to confirm cancellation windows.
3) For the On-demand per-token SKU, how are overage spikes handled in the console? Is there a daily cap option?

We'd like to move fast but need answers to these to prepare our PO.

Thanks —
Raj Patel
Head of AI Platforms, Acme Analytics
raj.patel@acme-analytics.com

-----Original Message-----
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme-analytics.com>, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Sarah Morris <sarah.morris@aws-partner.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace listing: product description and pricing Q&A

Raj — thanks for the clear questions. High level answers below; happy to hop on a 20-min call if you want to walk through with finance.

1) Invoice breakdown: Yes. For Dedicated we can provide a line-itemed invoice separating reserved GPU capacity (hours/instance type) and the Redwood platform fee. We'll include the template invoice as part of the co-sell brief.

2) Minimum term: Standard reserved commit is 12 months for the Dedicated SKU. We can negotiate shorter pilot terms as part of an enterprise addendum — Marcus and I will coordinate if Acme wants a 3-month pilot contract.

3) Overages & caps: For On-demand (per-token) we offer optional daily and monthly spend caps configurable at the account level. Marketplace purchases will default to the SKU's billing; customers can configure caps once the account is provisioned — we'll include a support article link in the listing.

Action items:
- Marcus: please prepare the 1-page partner brief and a pricing doc link (S3) for Marketplace ops.
- Karthik: confirm the unit mapping for embedding vs. generation pricing in pricing_table_v3.csv.
- Lauren: finalize the 72-word short description and update the doc for Sarah's 60-80 word constraint.

If there are no compliance flags from Marketplace ops by Thursday EOD we'll publish the draft.

Best —
Jasmine
